queue.tree_name: The Copper Beech of the Antonius Abtkerk
queue.recognise: You can recognise it by its near-black, red-purple leaves. It stands on the boundary of the Sint Antonius Abtkerk and its rectory on Dennenstraat, older than the church beside it.
queue.story:
This copper beech is older than the church beside it. The current Sint Antonius Abtkerk on Dennenstraat, a red-brick building by the architect Pieter Cuypers, went up in 1879 and 1880. The national register places the beech at the boundary of the church and its rectory somewhere between 1750 and 1800, roughly a century older than the bricks next to it.

That is not as strange as it sounds. The parish itself predates Cuypers by centuries. An older church stood on this ground before his, a barn chapel was rebuilt here in 1826, and parish history traces the site back to a sixteenth century predecessor. A beech planted in the late 1700s would have grown up beside whatever building stood here the
queue.name: The Copper Beech of the Antonius Abtkerk
